facts.text: CE marking is a manufacturer's declaration that a product meets European Union law; a notified body is an independent organization appointed by authorities to check high-risk products before CE marking.
facts.quote: CE marking is the label a manufacturer puts on a product to declare that it meets European Union law, and a notified body is an independent organization appointed by the authorities to check high-risk products before that label may be applied.

facts.text: CE marking is not a quality award: it is the manufacturer's own signed statement that the product complies with every applicable European Union law and that a technical file proves compliance.
facts.quote: They are the manufacturer's own signed statement that the product complies with every European Union (EU) law that applies to it and that a technical file proves it.

facts.text: Applying CE marking is the last step of conformity assessment; for most machinery, the manufacturer performs the entire assessment alone, using harmonized standards where available.
facts.quote: Applying the mark is the last step of conformity assessment, and for most machinery the manufacturer does the whole assessment alone, using harmonized standards where they exist [Chapter 3].

facts.text: For products legally considered especially dangerous, a notified body must participate in conformity assessment. The notified body examines the design, documentation and sometimes the quality system, and issues a certificate required for CE marking.
facts.quote: It examines the design, the documentation and sometimes the quality system, and issues a certificate without which the product may not be CE marked.

facts.text: A notified body is a private test or certification organization assessed by an EU member state and notified to the European Commission as competent for a particular kind of product.
facts.quote: A notified body is a private test or certification organization that an EU member state has assessed and "notified" to the European Commission as competent for a kind of product.

facts.text: A notified body checks and certifies rather than approving a product as a type-approval authority would; the manufacturer still signs the compliance declaration.
facts.quote: It does not approve the product the way a type-approval authority does; it checks and certifies, and the manufacturer still signs.

facts.text: Annex I Part A of Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 includes safety components with fully or partially self-evolving behaviour using machine learning approaches ensuring safety functions, and machinery embedding those components; every Part A conformity route involves a notified body.
facts.quote: "safety components with fully or partially self-evolving behaviour using machine learning approaches ensuring safety functions" and machinery embedding them; every conformity route for Part A involves a notified body [Chapters 1, 3].

facts.text: Whether a trained perception network frozen before delivery counts as “self-evolving” under Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 was disputed and unsettled in 2026.
facts.quote: Whether a trained perception network that is frozen before delivery counts as "self-evolving" is disputed and was unsettled in 2026 [Chapter 3].

facts.text: TÜV SÜD announced in September 2024 that it had become the first notified body under Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, establishing that the notified-body route exists.
facts.quote: TÜV SÜD announced in September 2024 that it had become the first notified body under the new regulation, so the route exists

facts.text: Notified-body positions on whether a frozen trained perception network counts as “self-evolving” under Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 were not found.
facts.quote: but notified-body positions on this question were not found [Chapter 13].

facts.text: Great Britain has the parallel UKCA (UK Conformity Assessed) mark and approved bodies, while Northern Ireland remains under EU product law.
facts.quote: Great Britain has a parallel mark, UKCA (UK Conformity Assessed), and "approved bodies"; Northern Ireland stays under EU product law [Chapter 3].

facts.text: A machine first sold in mid-2027 falls under Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, which applies from 20 January 2027.
facts.quote: A machine first sold in mid-2027 falls under the Machinery Regulation from 20 January 2027.

facts.text: If machine learning performs the braking function, the conservative program plan budgets for notified-body involvement.
facts.quote: If machine learning performs the braking function, the conservative plan budgets for notified-body involvement

facts.text: Notified-body lead time alone could exceed the program's four-month validation window; the notified-body lead time was not found.
facts.quote: the booklet warns that notified-body lead time alone could exceed the four-month validation window, with that lead time not found [Chapters 1, 3].

facts.text: Whether any notified body will accept simulation evidence for machinery conformity was not found.
facts.quote: Whether any notified body will accept simulation evidence for machinery conformity was also not found

facts.text: A safety channel without machine learning could change the machinery conformity route.
facts.quote: a safety channel without machine learning could change the route [Chapter 13].
